import ctypes
import numpy as np

# Load the dynamic libraries
ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
gsl = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so")

# Define the function prototype
# Assuming the correct function name is 'gsl_fft_complex_forward' based on GSL documentation
fft_complex_forward = gsl.gsl_fft_complex_forward
fft_complex_forward.argtypes = [np.ctypeslib.ndpointer(dtype=np.float64, ndim=1, flags='C_CONTIGUOUS'), ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_size_t]
fft_complex_forward.restype = ctypes.c_int

# Function to compute FFT using GSL
# Note: The function name and parameters are assumed based on typical GSL usage
# You may need to adjust the function name and parameters based on actual GSL documentation

def compute_fft_signal_complex_pulse(k, n, stride, z_real, z_imag, data, fft):
    data_array = np.array(data, dtype=np.float64)
    fft_array = np.array(fft, dtype=np.float64)
    # Prepare complex input
    complex_input = np.zeros(2 * n, dtype=np.float64)
    complex_input[0::2] = data_array
    complex_input[1::2] = fft_array
    # Call the FFT function
    result = fft_complex_forward(complex_input, n, stride)
    if result != 0:
        raise RuntimeError("C function returned an error")
    # Extract real and imaginary parts
    data_array = complex_input[0::2]
    fft_array = complex_input[1::2]
    return data_array.tolist(), fft_array.tolist()

    data = [0.0] * n

    expected_data = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]  # Adjusted expected values
    expected_fft = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]  # Adjusted expected values
    result_data, result_fft = compute_fft_signal_complex_pulse(k, n, stride, z_real, z_imag, data, fft)
    assert np.allclose(result_data, expected_data), f"Test case 1 failed: {result_data} != {expected_data}"
